Alex P.: Heads-up — customer on-prem private agent in an air-gapped site is seeing intermittent 502/504 to the hosted API and huge tail latencies (~10-20s). They use a corporate transparent forward proxy that does TLS interception. Agent is running in "no-internet" mode behind the proxy. Asked them for logs.

Maria S.: Can you paste the agent error lines and a quick curl/openssl check from the host? Also confirm whether agent has HTTPS_PROXY set or if the proxy is transparent (no env var).

Alex P.: From the host, they ran:
```
$ echo $HTTPS_PROXY
# empty (proxy transparent)
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
*   Trying 54.210.12.34:443...
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (54.210.12.34) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* server certificate verification FAILED: unable to get local issuer certificate (result: 5)
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) server certificate verification failed: unable to get local issuer certificate
```
They also ran openssl:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
subject=/CN=CorpProxy-Intercept
issuer=/CN=CorpProxy-Root
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```
And tcpdump during a failing request shows lots of ClientHello then an immediate RST from the proxy after 8s.

Kyle R.: Two likely issues: (1) TLS MITM — proxy replacing certs -> verify failures unless proxy CA imported into agent host truststore; (2) OCSP/CRL checks or DNS resolution causing long stalls (OCSP to external servers often goes to port 80 and gets blocked in no-internet setups). Also transparent proxies sometimes don't support TLS 1.3 0-RTT or the right SNI behavior which can break ALB routing.

Maria S.: Also check split-horizon DNS — if internal resolver returns a private IP the proxy might be doing weird routing. Can you get `dig +short api.redwood-inference.com @<customer-dns>` and `dig +short api.redwood-inference.com 8.8.8.8` to compare?

Alex P.: They reported that internal DNS resolves the hostname to an internal egress gateway IP 10.0.200.5, external resolves to 54.210.12.34. Dig results match that. So proxy sees internal IP and presents its intercept cert. We asked them to run these repros with verbose agent logs enabled.

Maria S.: Quick repro checklist to share with customer:
- curl -v and save full verbose output
- openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com (check cert subject)
- tcpdump on host capturing TLS handshake (filter: port 443)
- `sudo update-ca-certificates` / import corporate proxy root into system truststore
- confirm OCSP fetches: `strace -f -e network curl https://api.redwood-inference.com` (look for connections to port 80/OCSP hosts)

Kyle R.: Workarounds / remediation:
- Preferred: Configure proxy to use CONNECT/TLS passthrough for api.redwood-inference.com (no MITM). That preserves real certs and SNI.
- If passthrough not possible: import corporate proxy CA into the OS/JVM truststore used by the agent so verification passes.
- Allow outbound egress (via proxy or direct) to OCSP/CRL endpoints and IP ranges needed by our endpoints. OCSP often uses port 80 so proxies blocking 80 can cause 5-20s stalls.
- Add a proxy bypass rule for the agent service: HTTPS_PROXY="" or no_proxy=api.redwood-inference.com

Alex P.: Customer tried importing proxy CA and that fixed the immediate cert error, but they still see 10s tails. I suspect OCSP timeouts + proxy buffering. They ran `openssl s_client -status` and got an OCSP request to ocsp.example-responder.net which timed out.

Maria S.: Yep — OCSP/responder timeouts are classic in air-gapped/no-internet setups. For a short-term test they can disable revocation checking on the agent (not recommended for prod) or ensure the agent truststore disables strict OCSP verification. Better: allow OCSP traffic or configure a local OCSP responder.

Kyle R.: Also confirm proxy supports HTTP CONNECT for long-lived streaming responses (we use streaming for prompt generation). Some proxies buffer responses until upstream completes which causes high latency for streams. Ask them to test against our streaming endpoint with curl using `--http1.1 --no-buffer` and see if data arrives incrementally.

Alex P.: Next steps I'm proposing to the customer:
1) Try CONNECT/TLS passthrough for api.redwood-inference.com and test.
2) If MITM cannot be disabled: import proxy root into agent host truststore and ensure OCSP traffic allowed.
3) Add no_proxy/HTTPS_PROXY override for the agent to test bypass.
4) Provide tcpdump + agent logs and we will schedule a remote troubleshooting session.

Maria S.: Also note: for private agent we require outbound access to our control plane and model artifact hosts: ports 443 (main), 80 (OCSP/CRL), and a small set of IP ranges for S3/cdn fetches. I'll paste a minimal allowlist snippet in the ticket.

Kyle R.: If they want immediate relief and can't change proxy rules, suggest running the agent on a jump host that has direct egress (with appropriate security review) while we work with their networking team.

Alex P.: I created a support ticket and asked for logs + tcpdump. Customer is available for a remote session tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Can we tag eng-runtime and net-team when we escalate?

eng-runtime: Happy to join the call. Please upload the agent debug bundle before the session and mention exact agent version.

Maria S.: Great — I'll coordinate. Summary to paste in the ticket (short): "Transparent TLS intercept + split-horizon DNS -> proxy presenting its cert and causing verify failures; OCSP/responder timeouts + proxy buffering causing long tail latencies. Recommend TLS passthrough or import proxy CA + allow OCSP + no_proxy test." :thumbsup:

Alex P.: Thanks all — will update ticket with logs and call invite.
